subject: Science
stem: A push or a pull that can change the state of motion of an object, or change its shape, is called:
explanation: Force is any push or pull that can start, stop, speed up, slow down, change the direction of motion, or deform an object.

subject: Science
stem: A sharp knife cuts a vegetable more easily than a blunt one, even when the same force is applied, because the sharp knife has a:

options.option_text: Smaller surface area at the edge, producing greater pressure for the same force
Larger surface area at the edge, producing greater pressure
Higher weight than the blunt knife
Lower density than the blunt knife

explanation: Pressure = Force / Area. A sharper edge concentrates the same force over a much smaller area, producing much higher pressure — this is why knives, needles, and nails are made with fine points/edges.

subject: Science
stem: A block sliding on a rough floor gradually slows down and stops, even though no one is pushing it backward. The force responsible for opposing its motion and bringing it to rest is:
explanation: Friction is the opposing force that acts between two surfaces in contact, resisting relative motion — it is why a moving object on a rough surface eventually slows and stops without any external retarding push.

subject: Science
stem: A car moving on a straight highway shows one type of motion, while the tip of a clock's second hand shows another. These two types of motion are respectively called:

options.option_text: Uniform motion and Non-uniform motion only

explanation: Rectilinear motion is movement along a straight path; circular motion is movement along a circular path at a fixed distance from a centre point — these are classified by the PATH of motion, distinct from uniform/non-uniform (which classify by SPEED).

subject: Science
stem: A train covers equal distances in equal intervals of time throughout its journey, while a car in city traffic covers unequal distances in equal time intervals. These are respectively examples of:
explanation: Uniform motion covers equal distances in equal time intervals (constant speed); non-uniform motion covers unequal distances in equal time intervals (changing speed), as in stop-start city traffic.

subject: Science
stem: The pressure exerted by the column of air present in the atmosphere on the Earth's surface is called atmospheric pressure. At higher altitudes (e.g., on a mountain), atmospheric pressure is:

options.option_text: Lower than at sea level, because there is less air column above
Exactly the same as at sea level

explanation: Atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude because there is progressively less air column above pressing down — this is why mountaineers experience thinner air and lower pressure at high altitudes.
